## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 22 user-facing changes.
### New
- Choose how the address field shows a page's address in Appearance: on two lines, on one line, or just the site. - Super Copy, on by default, copies and shares links without known trackers. It follows supported redirect links to their destination, applies AdGuard's URL Tracking filter and Crest's own rules, and shortens Amazon product links. Selecting the address and copying it keeps everything. - Choose how the address field, pins, extensions, selected tab and other glass surfaces read in Appearance: Automatic follows each Space, dark over dark Spaces and light over very light ones, or keep them Light, Dark, or as your Mac's appearance (System). - On Mac, closing a Quick Window that opened over another app, from one of its links or the New Quick Window shortcut, takes you back to that app. Crest's other windows stay behind that app while the Quick Window is open.
### Improved
- The sidebar narrows to 164 points, about as narrow as Arc's. In a narrow sidebar, Forward folds away to keep clear of the window's buttons, and Copy URL makes room for the address. - On macOS 27, Settings pages other than Shortcuts and Feature Flags scroll wherever the pointer is, with the scroll bar at the edge of the page, while their settings stay in a column down the middle.
### Fixed
- Copy URL and Site Controls sit side by side in the address field instead of on top of each other. - A folder inside a closed folder opens when you click it, showing everything in it while the folder around it stays closed. - The Start Page title on the Mac reads in its Space's light or dark look, so it no longer draws black over a dark Space. - In a narrow sidebar, Copy URL appears in the address field while the pointer is over it, so you can still copy the address with a click. - On Mac, a Quick Window that a link from another app or the New Quick Window shortcut opens appears over the app you're using, on the display you're using it on, instead of over another app's window. Links in Crest's own Settings open over Crest. - An isolated test copy of Crest on Mac keeps its own sidebar width, opening at the default and never changing the installed app's.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.51, which fixes CVE-2026-125350, a security flaw being exploited in the wild, and eight other security flaws.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
